newsitem.title: FRANCE: French insurer Axa's profits jump pre-merger.
newsitem.headline: French insurer Axa's profits jump pre-merger.

text.p: French insurer Axa, which is merging with rival French group UAP to create the world's second largest insurance company, said Wednesday 1996 profits rocketed 40 percent.
Axa's net attributable profit soared to 3.81 billion francs ($670 million) from 2.73 billion ($417 million) as revenues rose 28 percent to 167.21 billion ($29.4 billion).

Clearing the decks for the merger, UAP reported a loss of 6.45 billion francs ($1.13 billion) after writing off 7.59 billion francs ($1.33 billion) in one-time charges to purge its books and prevent money-losing activities weighing on the new group's future.

Excluding the one-time charges, which included businesses in a collapsed property sector, UAP's profit was 1.14 billion francs ($200.5 million). UAP had a net attributable loss of 2.1 billion francs ($369.5 million) in 1995.
"UAP is a good company which probably made investments that were a little risky in the past," Axa Chairman Claude Bebear, who is heading the new group, told reporters.
"We have taken the last necessary provisions to erase what was done in the past," he said, adding he was confident about the new group's future. "Things are going well."

Axa and UAP, France's two largest insurers, are integrating their operations to form Axa-UAP after a surprise announcement in November that they would combine to create a French heavyweight in the global insurance business. The group will be known commercially as Axa.
